questions.question: What type of reproduction is used by flowering plants to produce seeds?
options: Asexual reproduction
Sexual reproduction
Binary fission
Budding

questions.question: Why is plant reproduction vital for all animal life on Earth?
options: Plants produce carbon dioxide for animals to breathe
Plants are producers that provide the primary source of food
Plants warm up the Earth's atmosphere
Plants absorb excess water from the soil

questions.question: Which statement is true about the reproductive organs of flowers?
options: Flowers only contain male sex organs
Flowers only contain female sex organs
Flowers contain both male and female sex organs and gametes
Flowers contain neither male nor female sex organs

questions.question: What is the name of the female gamete in flowering plants?
options: Pollen grain
Anther
Stigma
Egg cell (ova)

questions.question: What do pollen grains carry in flowering plants?
options: Female gametes
Male gametes
Embryos
Food stores

questions.question: Which three components make up a seed, and where are seeds formed?
options: Pollen, ovary, and stem; formed in the anther
Embryo, food store, and tough outer coat; formed in the ovary
Root, leaf, and bud; formed in the petals
Zygote, nectar, and style; formed in the stigma

questions.question: What biologically defines a fruit in seed-producing plants?
options: A sweet-tasting leaf
The mature and ripened ovary
The swollen tip of a root
A protective layer of pollen

questions.question: What are three main natural agents that seeds are adapted to be dispersed by?
options: Animals, wind, and water
Fire, soil, and sunlight
Insects, birds, and worms
Gravity, electricity, and magnetism

questions.question: What is the primary role of a pollinator in plant reproduction?
options: To digest the seeds of the plant
To protect the flower from harsh weather
To transfer pollen from one flower to another
To absorb nutrients from the soil for the plant

questions.question: Which group represents the majority of animal pollinators, with bees being the largest group within it?
options: Mammals
Birds
Insects
Reptiles

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'food security'?
options: Locking up food in secure storage facilities
Having enough affordable and nutritious food in an area or country
Importing all food from other nations
Using only artificial chemicals to grow crops

questions.question: Which of the following threats must pollinating insects be protected from to ensure future food security?
options: Pesticides, climate change, and habitat loss
High oxygen levels and strong sunlight
Organic farming and wildflower planting
Natural rain and wind patterns

questions.question: What is pollination?
options: The growth of a seed into a young seedling
The fusion of male and female gametes in the ovary
The transfer of pollen from the male anther to the female stigma
The release of seeds from a ripe fruit

questions.question: What is a major genetic advantage of cross-pollination compared to self-pollination?
options: It requires less energy from the plant
It increases variation in a species
It guarantees that no seeds are produced
It occurs without the need for gametes

questions.question: What occurs during the process of fertilisation in plants?
options: The transfer of pollen to a different flower by wind
The fusion of the nuclei from the male and female gametes
The shedding of petals after pollination
The absorption of water by a dry seed

questions.question: In a plant investigation, when should you display your data using a bar chart instead of a line graph?
options: When the independent variable is continuous
When the independent variable is categoric
When you have only two data points
When the dependent variable is extremely large

questions.question: Which of the following is a common seed used in school labs that will germinate on damp cotton wool under the right conditions?
options: Oak seeds
Cress seeds
Coconut seeds
Avocado seeds

questions.question: When planning an investigation into seed germination, what is the 'dependent variable'?
options: The factor you choose to change, such as temperature
The factors you keep the same to ensure a fair test
The variable you measure to conclude on the effect
The type of seeds you use in the experiment

questions.question: Why must we identify and control variables (keep them the same) during a seed germination investigation?
options: To make the experiment run as fast as possible
To ensure we can draw a valid conclusion
To change the results to match our prediction
To avoid having to repeat the measurements

questions.question: How are wind-dispersed seeds typically adapted to match their mechanism of dispersal?
options: They are heavy with a sticky outer surface
They are enclosed in bright, fleshy fruits
They are light with a large surface area
They have sharp hooks to cling to passing objects
